chunks: Sa'd from Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from Fadala, from Hammad ibn ʿUthman, from Abu Usama Zayd al-Shahham, who said: I heard Abu ʿAbdillah (peace be upon him) say:
"A man shortens the salat on a journey of twelve miles."

key_terms.مَسِيرَةِ: journey / travel distance; the measured span of travel triggering legal rulings
key_terms.مِيلًا: mile (mayal); classical unit of distance, approx. 1.6–1.9 km
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: shortens (the prayer); technical term for qasr, the traveller's shortened salat

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum travel distance in miles for shortening salat according to Imam al-Sadiq in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Jaʿfar al-Sadiq (AS) establishes twelve miles (amyal) as the minimum travel distance at which a man shortens (qasr) his salat. Transmitted through a reliable Qummi chain, it is one of several narrations compiled by Shaykh al-Tusi in al-Istibsar's chapter on the obligatory travel distance for qasr prayer, which the author uses to reconcile differing transmitted measures.
